title: Block whole-person body and environment spatial merges
starting_state: A doorway proof has correct text, people count, hand count, and style, but Zuv's shoulder/back/torso visually merges into the door plane.
The visual QA artifact claims PASS because broad anatomy and identity checks passed while whole-person spatial topology is broken.
done_when: Every person has a traceable silhouette and explicit front/back relationship to nearby solid objects.
A body region that morphs into a door, wall, chair, bed, sofa, frame, or table blocks proof approval.
Valid single-point contact or clear occlusion still passes when the body continues visibly and depth order is explained.
forbidden_changes: Do not treat correct people, arms, hands, or fingers as sufficient spatial QA.
Do not allow a body to merge into a solid object because the watercolor edge looks soft.
Do not ban valid occlusion or leaning contact when depth order and body continuation are explicit.
fail_to_pass: the Zuv-inside-door spatial-topology fixture is rejected even when people and hand counts are correct
pass_to_pass: a continuous person silhouette with valid single-point contact or clear occlusion passes spatial topology
anti_gaming_notes: Hidden variants should change the person, body region, object, camera angle, and valid occlusion control so the checker cannot key only on Zuv or door.
